options.label: Hemisphere
options.summary: Create a 1-foot-thick hemispherical ice dome with a radius of up to 10 feet on a solid surface.

options.label: Globe
options.summary: Create a 1-foot-thick ice globe with a radius of up to 10 feet on a solid surface.

options.label: Flat Contiguous Panels
options.summary: Create up to ten contiguous 10-foot-square ice panels on a solid surface.

modeChoice.notes: The form is a casting-time branch, and cut-through creature push direction remains a caster choice when the wall appears.

wall-of-ice.description: You create a wall of ice on a solid surface within range. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-square panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1 foot thick and lasts for the duration. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side) and makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The wall is an object that can be damaged and thus breached. It has AC 12 and 30 Hit Points per 10-foot section, and it has Immunity to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage and Vulnerability to Fire damage. Reducing a 10-foot section of wall to 0 Hit Points destroys it and leaves behind a sheet of frigid air in the space the wall occupied. A creature moving through the sheet of frigid air for the first time on a turn makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
wall-of-ice.higherLevels: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage the wall deals when it appears increases by 2d6 and the damage from passing through the sheet of frigid air increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 6.

wall-of-light.name: Wall of Light

forms.label: Wall of Light
forms.notes: The wall can be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.

saveOutcomeOverrides.effect: The creature takes half Radiant damage and is not Blinded.
The creature takes full Radiant damage and is Blinded for 1 minute.

recurringMechanics.notes: A creature that ends its turn in the wall's area takes Radiant damage; this recurring damage is separate from the initial save when the wall appears.

effects.description: When the 60-foot-long, 10-foot-high, 5-foot-thick wall appears at a point within 120 feet, each creature in the wall makes a Constitution save, taking 4d8 Radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success; each slot level above 5 adds +1d8 damage.

grantedActions.notes: Until the spell ends, the caster can use an action to launch a beam of radiance from the wall at one visible creature within 60 feet of it. On hit, the target takes 4d8 Radiant damage; hit or miss, the wall length is reduced by 10 feet.

conditionalEndings.description: Whether the radiant beam hits or misses, wall length drops by 10 feet; if it reaches 0 feet, the spell ends.

effects.description: A creature that fails the wall's initial Constitution save is Blinded for 1 minute and can repeat the Constitution save at the end of each turn, ending the Blinded effect on a success.

conditionalEndings.description: Whether the radiant beam hits or misses, wall length drops by 10 feet; if it reaches 0 feet, the spell ends.

effects.description: Creates a shimmering wall of bright light that blocks line of sight while allowing creatures and objects to pass through it.

createdObjects.name: Wall of Light
createdObjects.notes: A 60-foot-long, 10-foot-high, 5-foot-thick shimmering light wall. It blocks line of sight, does not block passage, emits bright and dim light, damages creatures that end their turn in its area, and can shrink by 10 feet whenever the caster launches a radiant beam.

conditionalEndings.description: Whether the radiant beam hits or misses, wall length drops by 10 feet; if it reaches 0 feet, the spell ends.

visionLightSound.wallDimensions: up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, 5 feet thick
visionLightSound.blindOnFailedSave: initial Constitution save failure Blinds for 1 minute with end-turn repeats
visionLightSound.beam: caster can launch radiant beam at visible creature within 60 feet of wall, reducing wall length by 10 feet

aiContext.prompt: Choose the wall orientation and point, resolve Constitution saves for creatures in the wall when it appears, track Blinded repeat saves at turn end, apply Radiant damage to creatures ending in the wall, and reduce wall length by 10 feet whenever the caster fires a radiant beam.

wall-of-light.description: A shimmering wall of bright light appears at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose: horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. It can be free floating, or it can rest on a solid surface. The wall can be up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight, but creatures and objects can pass through it. It emits bright light out to 120 feet and dim light for an additional 120 feet. When the wall appears, each creature in its area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d8 radiant damage, and it is blinded for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't blinded. A blinded creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that ends its turn in the wall's area takes 4d8 radiant damage. Until the spell ends, you can use an action to launch a beam of radiance from the wall at one creature you can see within 60 feet of it. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 4d8 radiant damage. Whether you hit or miss, reduce the length of the wall by 10 feet. If the wall's length drops to 0 feet, the spell ends.
wall-of-light.higherLevels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 5th.

wall-of-sand.name: Wall of Sand

movementCostModifier.description: A creature moving through the wall's space must spend 3 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves there.

effects.description: Creatures in the 30-foot-long, 10-foot-high, 10-foot-thick sand wall gain the Blinded condition for up to 10 minutes with concentration; the wall blocks line of sight but not movement, and each foot moved inside costs 3 feet of movement.

createdObjects.name: Wall Of Sand
createdObjects.notes: Wall of Sand rises from the ground as a 30-foot by 10-foot by 10-foot wall; creatures in its space are blinded and spend 3 feet of movement for each 1 foot moved there.

aiContext.prompt: Place the sand wall; while a creature is in the wall's space, apply Blinded and charge 3 feet of movement for every 1 foot moved through the wall.

wall-of-sand.description: You conjure up a wall of swirling sand on the ground at a point you can see within range. You can make the wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 10 feet thick, and it vanishes when the spell ends. It blocks line of sight but not movement. A creature is blinded while in the wall's space and must spend 3 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves there.

wall-of-stone.name: Wall of Stone

saveOutcomeOverrides.effect: The creature can use its Reaction to move up to its Speed so it is no longer enclosed.

effects.description: Create a nonmagical stone wall for up to 10 minutes with concentration as ten contiguous 10-foot-by-10-foot panels, or as thinner 10-foot-by-20-foot panels. The wall can form supported shapes such as bridges, ramps, battlements, or similar stonework; a creature enclosed by the wall can make a Dexterity save to use its Reaction and move up to its Speed to escape enclosure. Each panel is a damageable stone object with AC 15, 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; destroyed panels can cause connected sections to collapse at the DM discretion, and full-duration concentration makes the wall permanent and unable to be dispelled.

enclosureEscapeSave.success: Creature can use its Reaction to move up to its Speed so it is no longer enclosed.

createdObjects.name: Wall of Stone
createdObjects.shelfLife: 10 minutes unless concentration is maintained for the full duration
createdObjects.notes: Ten contiguous stone panels. Standard panels are 10 by 10 feet and 6 inches thick; the caster can instead use 10-by-20-foot panels that are 3 inches thick. Each panel has AC 15 and 30 HP per inch of thickness, is immune to Poison and Psychic damage, can be breached, and may become permanent after full-duration concentration.

aiContext.prompt: Choose panel layout, height/thickness option, support/anchoring, and pushed side for creatures in spaces the wall cuts through. If any creature would be fully enclosed, resolve its Dexterity save and Reaction movement before finalizing enclosure.

wall-of-stone.description: A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side). If a creature would be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall and another solid surface), that creature can make a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no longer enclosed by the wall. The wall can have any shape you desire, though it can't occupy the same space as a creature or object. The wall doesn't need to be vertical or rest on a firm foundation. It must, however, merge with and be solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp. If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length, you must halve the size of each panel to create supports. You can crudely shape the wall to create battlements and the like. The wall is an object made of stone that can be damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15 and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause connected panels to collapse at the DM's discretion. If you maintain your Concentration on this spell for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent and can't be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disappears when the spell ends.

durationProgression.notes: Maintaining concentration on Wall of Stone for its full duration makes the wall permanent and unable to be dispelled.

wall-of-thorns.name: Wall of Thorns

effects.description: When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity save, taking 7d8 Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
The first time a creature enters a space in the wall on a turn, it makes a Dexterity save, taking 7d8 Slashing damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
A creature that ends its turn in the wall makes a Dexterity save, taking 7d8 Slashing damage on a failed save or half as much on a success; this can happen only once per turn.
Create a thorn wall on a solid surface, up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick, that blocks line of sight for the spell duration.

createdObjects.name: Wall Of Thorns
createdObjects.notes: Wall of Thorns appears on a solid surface, blocks line of sight, and costs 4 feet of movement for each foot moved through it.

effects.description: For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement.

Create a thorn wall for up to 10 minutes with concentration as a straight wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick, or as a circular wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick.

controlOptions.name: Straight Wall Form
controlOptions.effect: The wall can be up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick.

controlOptions.name: Circular Wall Form
controlOptions.effect: The wall can be a circle with a 20-foot diameter, up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick.

controlOptions.name: Blocks Line Of Sight
controlOptions.effect: The wall blocks line of sight.

controlOptions.name: Slow Movement Through Wall
controlOptions.effect: For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement.

wall-of-thorns.description: You create a wall of tangled brush bristling with needle-sharp thorns. The wall appears within range on a solid surface and lasts for the duration. You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick or a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight. When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 7d8 Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature can move through the wall, albeit slowly and painfully. For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement. Furthermore, the first time a creature enters a space in the wall on a turn or ends its turn there, the creature makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 7d8 Slashing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature makes this save only once per turn.
wall-of-thorns.higherLevels: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Both types of damage increase by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 6.

wall-of-water.name: Wall of Water

effects.description: Creates a straight or ringed water wall whose space is Difficult Terrain, imposes Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks crossing it, halves Fire damage crossing it, and can freeze into destructible 5-foot sections when Cold spells pass through.

createdObjects.name: Wall of Water
createdObjects.notes: A wall of water on the ground. It can be a straight wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ring up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. Its space is difficult terrain, ranged weapon attacks through it have disadvantage, Fire damage through it is halved, and Cold damage through it freezes at least one 5-foot square section with AC 5 and 15 HP.

aiContext.prompt: Choose straight wall or ring shape; while the wall lasts, mark its space as difficult terrain, give ranged weapon attacks Disadvantage when they enter the wall, halve Fire damage that passes through it, and track Cold-damage frozen sections.

wall-of-water.description: You create a wall of water on the ground at a point you can see within range. You can make the wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or you can make a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall vanishes when the spell ends. The wall's space is difficult terrain. Any ranged weapon attack that enters the wall's space has disadvantage on the attack roll, and fire damage is halved if the fire effect passes through the wall to reach its target. Spells that deal cold damage that pass through the wall cause the area of the wall they pass through to freeze solid (at least a 5-foot-square section is frozen). Each 5-foot-square frozen section has AC 5 and 15 hit points. Reducing a frozen section to 0 hit points destroys it. When a section is destroyed, the wall's water doesn't fill it.

warding-bond.name: Warding Bond

components.materialDescription: a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear for the duration

savingThrow.notes: While the Warding Bond target remains within 60 feet of the caster, it gains +1 to saving throws.

effects.description: The willing touched target gains a +1 bonus to AC for 1 hour while the Warding Bond link persists.
The willing touched target has Resistance to all damage for 1 hour while it remains within 60 feet of the caster.
While the link persists (within 60 ft), you take the same amount of damage the target takes. Ends if either drops to 0 HP or you exceed 60 ft separation.

conditionalEndings.description: The spell ends if the caster drops to 0 Hit Points.
The spell ends if the caster and target become separated by more than 60 feet.
The spell ends if Warding Bond is cast again on either connected creature.

aiContext.prompt: Ask the caster to choose a willing other creature wearing the paired ring; while within 60 feet, apply +1 AC, +1 saving throws, all-damage Resistance, and mirrored damage to the caster.

warding-bond.description: You touch another creature that is willing and create a mystic connection between you and the target until the spell ends. While the target is within 60 feet of you, it gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws, and it has Resistance to all damage. Also, each time it takes damage, you take the same amount of damage. The spell ends if you drop to 0 Hit Points or if you and the target become separated by more than 60 feet. It also ends if the spell is cast again on either of the connected creatures.

water-breathing.name: Water Breathing

requirements.description: The ritual must be chanted aloud from start to finish.
The ritual needs a free hand for its gestures throughout.
The ritual needs a short reed; it is held throughout the casting.
Ritual casting adds 10 minutes to the casting time and must run uninterrupted.

effects.description: Up to ten chosen creatures within range can breathe underwater for 24 hours while retaining their normal respiration.

respirationState.notes: Water Breathing gives chosen willing creatures underwater respiration while preserving their normal breathing mode, so the creature can function both underwater and in air during the spell.

water-breathing.description: This spell grants up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range the ability to breathe underwater until the spell ends. Affected creatures also retain their normal mode of respiration.

water-walk.name: Water Walk

requirements.description: The ritual must be chanted aloud from start to finish.
The ritual needs a free hand for its gestures throughout.
The ritual needs a piece of cork; it is held throughout the casting.
Ritual casting adds 10 minutes to the casting time and must run uninterrupted.

effects.description: Choose up to ten creatures within 30 feet for 1 hour. Targets can move across liquid surfaces as harmless solid ground and can use a Bonus Action to pass between a liquid's surface and the liquid itself, while falling into the liquid bypasses that Bonus Action requirement.

grantedActions.action: Pass between the liquid's surface and the liquid itself, or vice versa.
grantedActions.notes: Falling into the liquid bypasses this Bonus Action requirement and passes the target through the surface into the liquid below.

liquidSurfaceMovement.notes: Water Walk changes how chosen creatures interact with liquid surfaces without making those liquids harmless for all purposes; lava heat damage still applies.

surfaceInteraction.notes: Targets can move across liquid surfaces as harmless solid ground, but lava heat can still harm them and moving between the surface and liquid requires the spell-specific movement rule.

water-walk.description: This spell grants the ability to move across any liquid surface-such as water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, or lava-as if it were harmless solid ground (creatures crossing molten lava can still take damage from the heat). Up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range gain this ability for the duration. An affected target must take a Bonus Action to pass from the liquid's surface into the liquid itself and vice versa, but if the target falls into the liquid, the target passes through the surface into the liquid below.

watery-sphere.name: Watery Sphere

effects.description: Create the movable sphere of water so map and combat systems can track its hover limit, movement, occupant capacity, ejection rules, flame extinguish radius, and spell-end disappearance.

grantedActions.notes: Move the sphere up to 30 feet in a straight line; if it rams creatures, force the same Strength save.

createdObjects.name: Watery Sphere
createdObjects.notes: The sphere can hover up to 10 feet off the ground, move 30 feet in a straight line as an action, carry restrained occupants with it, eject overflow occupants at random, knock occupants prone when it falls at spell end, extinguish normal flames within 30 feet, and then vanish. The existing STATUS_CONDITION row owns the Strength save and Restrained application.

conditionalEndings.description: When the spell ends, the sphere falls, extinguishes normal flames within 30 feet, knocks restrained creatures prone where it falls, and the water vanishes.

saveOutcomeOverrides.reason: Huge or larger creatures automatically succeed on the Watery Sphere Strength save.
Large or smaller creatures can choose to fail the Watery Sphere Strength save.

effects.description: A Large or smaller creature in the 5-foot-radius water Sphere within 90 feet can choose to fail the Strength save; on a failed save it is Restrained and engulfed for up to 1 minute with concentration, moves with the sphere, repeats the Strength save at the end of each turn to escape, and is knocked Prone where the sphere falls when the spell ends. Huge or larger creatures automatically succeed.

conditionalEndings.description: When the spell ends, the sphere falls, extinguishes normal flames within 30 feet, knocks restrained creatures prone where it falls, and the water vanishes.

ejectionDestinationEligibility.notes: A creature that saves against entering the sphere is ejected to the nearest unoccupied outside space of its choice.

aiContext.prompt: Choose the sphere's origin point. For each affected creature, record whether it is Huge or larger and automatically succeeds, whether a Large or smaller creature chooses to fail, and where a successful creature chooses to be ejected outside the sphere.

watery-sphere.description: You conjure up a sphere of water with a 5-foot radius at a point you can see within range. The sphere can hover but no more than 10 feet off the ground. The sphere remains for the spell's duration. Any creature in the sphere's space must make a Strength saving throw. On a successful save, a creature is ejected from that space to the nearest unoccupied space of the creature's choice outside the sphere. A Huge or larger creature succeeds on the saving throw automatically, and a Large or smaller creature can choose to fail it. On a failed save, a creature is restrained by the sphere and is engulfed by the water. At the end of each of its turns, a restrained target can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. The sphere can restrain as many as four Medium or smaller creatures or one Large creature. If the sphere restrains a creature that causes it to exceed this capacity, a random creature that was already restrained by the sphere falls out of it and lands prone in a space within 5 feet of it. As an action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet in a straight line. If it moves over a pit, a cliff, or other drop-off, it safely descends until it is hovering 10 feet above the ground. Any creature restrained by the sphere moves with it. You can ram the sphere into creatures, forcing them to make the saving throw. When the spell ends, the sphere falls to the ground and extinguishes all normal flames within 30 feet of it. Any creature restrained by the sphere is knocked prone in the space where it falls. The water then vanishes.

web.name: Web

effects.description: Conjure a 20-foot Cube of sticky webbing that is Difficult Terrain, Lightly Obscured, anchored or layered against solid supports, and flammable.

createdObjects.name: Sticky Webbing
createdObjects.notes: The webs fill a 20-foot Cube, are Difficult Terrain and Lightly Obscured, collapse at the start of the caster's next turn if unsupported, and each ignited 5-foot Cube burns away in 1 round while dealing 2d4 Fire damage to creatures that start their turn in the fire.

conditionalEndings.description: A creature Restrained by the webs can use an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against the caster's spell save DC; on a success, it is no longer Restrained.
The Restrained condition lasts only while the creature is caught in the webs, so leaving or destroying the relevant webbing ends that target's restraint.

effects.description: Create a 20-foot Cube of sticky webs for up to 1 hour with concentration; the webbed area anchors restraint saves, Difficult Terrain, and burning-web damage.

conditionalEndings.description: If the webs are not anchored between solid masses or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself and the spell ends at the start of the caster's next turn.

effects.description: A creature that enters the webs or starts its turn there makes a Dexterity save; on a failure, it has the Restrained condition while caught in the webs.
If a 5-foot cube of web is ignited, the burning web is destroyed in 1 round and a creature that starts its turn in that burning area takes 2d4 Fire damage.
The webbed 20-foot Cube is Difficult Terrain for the spell duration.

aiContext.prompt: Ask the caster to place the 20-foot web cube and confirm its anchor or layered surface; prompt Dexterity saves when creatures enter or start in the webs, Strength (Athletics) escape checks for Restrained creatures, and 2d4 Fire damage for creatures starting in burning web cubes.

web.description: You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point within range. The webs fill a 20-foot Cube there for the duration. The webs are Difficult Terrain , and the area within them is Lightly Obscured . If the webs aren't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5 feet. The first time a creature enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Restrained condition while in the webs or until it breaks free. A creature Restrained by the webs can take an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained. The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot Cube of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.

weird.name: Weird

effects.description: Targets make a Wisdom save, taking 10d10 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
On a failed Wisdom save, the target is Frightened for up to 1 minute with concentration and repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on itself on a success.
A target still Frightened by Weird takes 5d10 Psychic damage when it fails the end-turn repeat Wisdom save.

Create illusory terrors in the minds of chosen creatures in a 30-foot-radius sphere within 120 feet for up to 1 minute with concentration. Affected creatures resolve Wisdom saves for the initial terror and for end-turn repeat pressure, with the spell ending on a target that succeeds on its repeat save.

controlOptions.name: Illusory terrors
controlOptions.effect: The caster creates illusory terrors in the minds of chosen creatures in the area.

controlOptions.name: Initial fright and damage
controlOptions.effect: A failed Wisdom save causes 10d10 Psychic damage and Frightened for the duration; success causes half damage only.

controlOptions.name: End-turn repeat save
controlOptions.effect: A Frightened target repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each turn.

controlOptions.name: Repeat damage or end
controlOptions.effect: On failed repeat saves the target takes 5d10 Psychic damage; on success the spell ends on that target.

weird.description: You try to create illusory terrors in others' minds. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 10d10 Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition for the duration. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. A Frightened target makes a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes 5d10 Psychic damage. On a successful save, the spell ends on that target.

whirlwind.name: Whirlwind

objectEligibility.notes: Whirlwind sucks up only Medium-or-smaller unsecured objects that are not worn or carried.

saveOutcomeOverrides.effect: The creature takes half Bludgeoning damage and avoids the follow-up Strength restraint save.
The creature takes full Bludgeoning damage; if Large or smaller, it must also make the Strength save against restraint.

effects.description: A creature makes a Dexterity save the first time on a turn it enters the whirlwind or the whirlwind enters its space, including when the whirlwind first appears; failed save takes 10d6 Bludgeoning damage, successful save takes half.

statusCondition.name: Restrained

escapeCheck.success: The creature is no longer Restrained and is hurled 3d6 x 10 feet in a random direction.

statusCondition.aftermath: A restrained creature moves with the whirlwind, is pulled 5 feet higher at the start of its turn unless at the top, falls when the spell ends unless it can stay aloft, and can escape with a Strength or Dexterity check.

effects.description: A Large or smaller creature that fails the Dexterity save must succeed on a Strength save or become Restrained in the whirlwind until the spell ends.
Until the spell ends, the caster can use an action to move the whirlwind up to 30 feet in any direction along the ground.
When a creature starts its turn Restrained by the whirlwind, it is pulled 5 feet higher inside it unless already at the top.

forcedMovement.maxDistance: fall when the spell ends unless able to stay aloft

effects.description: A restrained creature falls when the spell ends unless it has some means to stay aloft.
On a successful Strength or Dexterity escape check, the creature is no longer Restrained and is hurled 3d6 x 10 feet away in a random direction.

Creates a 10-foot-radius, 30-foot-high whirlwind on a visible ground point within 300 feet for up to 1 minute with concentration; the vortex can be moved along the ground, sucks up unsecured Medium-or-smaller objects that are not worn or carried, and its separate rows handle creature damage, restraint, upward pull, falling, and escape hurling.

grantedActions.name: Move Whirlwind
grantedActions.description: Move the whirlwind up to 30 feet in any direction along the ground.

controlOptions.name: Ground Point Whirlwind
controlOptions.effect: A 10-foot-radius, 30-foot-high Cylinder appears centered on a visible point on the ground within range.

controlOptions.name: Action Move Whirlwind
controlOptions.effect: Until the spell ends, you can use your action to move the whirlwind up to 30 feet in any direction along the ground.

controlOptions.name: Sucks Up Objects
controlOptions.effect: The whirlwind sucks up Medium or smaller objects that are not secured and are not worn or carried.

controlOptions.name: Entry Or Overlap Damage
controlOptions.effect: A creature saves the first time on a turn it enters the whirlwind or the whirlwind enters its space, including when the whirlwind first appears.

controlOptions.name: Large Or Smaller Restraint
controlOptions.effect: A Large or smaller creature that fails the Dexterity save must succeed on a Strength save or become Restrained in the whirlwind until the spell ends.

controlOptions.name: Restrained Pulled Upward
controlOptions.effect: When a creature starts its turn Restrained by the whirlwind, it is pulled 5 feet higher inside it unless already at the top.

controlOptions.name: Restrained Moves With Whirlwind
controlOptions.effect: A Restrained creature moves with the whirlwind.

controlOptions.name: Falls When Spell Ends
controlOptions.effect: A Restrained creature falls when the spell ends unless it has a way to stay aloft.

controlOptions.name: Escape Check
controlOptions.effect: A Restrained creature can use an action to make a Strength or Dexterity check against your spell save DC to end the restraint.

controlOptions.name: Escape Hurls Randomly
controlOptions.effect: On a successful escape check, the creature is hurled 3d6 x 10 feet away from the whirlwind in a random direction.

objectPickupEligibility.notes: The vortex can pick up Medium-or-smaller loose objects only when they are neither secured nor worn/carried.

aiContext.prompt: Place the 10-foot-radius, 30-foot-high whirlwind on visible ground. Track each creature's once-per-turn Dexterity save when it enters the whirlwind, the whirlwind enters its space, or the spell first appears; on failed Dexterity saves, resolve the Large-or-smaller Strength save for Restrained, upward pull, carried movement, fall on spell end, and Strength/Dexterity escape check.

whirlwind.description: A whirlwind howls down to a point that you can see on the ground within range. The whirlwind is a 10-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder centered on that point. Until the spell ends, you can use your action to move the whirlwind up to 30 feet in any direction along the ground. The whirlwind sucks up any Medium or smaller objects that aren't secured to anything and that aren't worn or carried by anyone. A creature must make a Dexterity saving throw the first time on a turn that it enters the whirlwind or that the whirlwind enters its space, including when the whirlwind first appears. A creature takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, a Large or smaller creature that fails the save must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become restrained in the whirlwind until the spell ends. When a creature starts its turn restrained by the whirlwind, the creature is pulled 5 feet higher inside it, unless the creature is at the top. A restrained creature moves with the whirlwind and falls when the spell ends, unless the creature has some means to stay aloft. A restrained creature can use an action to make a Strength or Dexterity check against your spell save DC. If successful, the creature is no longer restrained by the whirlwind and is hurled 3d6 x 10 feet away from it in a random direction.

wish.description: Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal can cast. By simply speaking aloud, you can alter reality itself. The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of level 8 or lower. If you use it this way, you don't need to meet any requirements to cast that spell, including costly components. The spell simply takes effect. Alternatively, you can create one of the following effects of your choice: Object Creation. You create one object of up to 25,000 GP in value that isn't a magic item. The object can be no more than 300 feet in any dimension, and it appears in an unoccupied space that you can see on the ground. Instant Health. You allow yourself and up to twenty creatures that you can see to regain all Hit Points, and you end all effects on them listed in the Greater Restoration spell. Resistance. You grant up to ten creatures that you can see Resistance to one damage type that you choose. This Resistance is permanent. Spell Immunity. You grant up to ten creatures you can see immunity to a single spell or other magical effect for 8 hours. Sudden Learning. You replace one of your feats with another feat for which you are eligible. You lose all the benefits of the old feat and gain the benefits of the new one. You can't replace a feat that is a prerequisite for any of your other feats or features. Roll Redo. You undo a single recent event by forcing a reroll of any die roll made within the last round (including your last turn). Reality reshapes itself to accommodate the new result. For example, a Wish spell could undo an ally's failed saving throw or a foe's Critical Hit. You can force the reroll to be made with Advantage or Disadvantage, and you choose whether to use the reroll or the original roll. Reshape Reality. You may wish for something not included in any of the other effects. To do so, state your wish to the DM as precisely as possible. The DM has great latitude in ruling what occurs in such an instance; the greater the wish, the greater the likelihood that something goes wrong. This spell might simply fail, the effect you desire might be achieved only in part, or you might suffer an unforeseen consequence as a result of how you worded the wish. For example, wishing that a villain were dead might propel you forward in time to a period when that villain is no longer alive, effectively removing you from the game. Similarly, wishing for a Legendary magic item or an Artifact might instantly transport you to the presence of the item's current owner. If your wish is granted and its effects have consequences for a whole community, region, or world, you are likely to attract powerful foes. If your wish would affect a god, the god's divine servants might instantly intervene to prevent it or to encourage you to craft the wish in a particular way. If your wish would undo the multiverse itself, threaten the City of Sigil, or affect the Lady of Pain in any way, you see an image of her in your mind for a moment; she shakes her head, and your wish fails. The stress of casting Wish to produce any effect other than duplicating another spell weakens you. After enduring that stress, each time you cast a spell until you finish a Long Rest, you take 1d10 Necrotic damage per level of that spell. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way. In addition, your Strength score becomes 3 for 2d4 days. For each of those days that you spend resting and doing nothing more than light activity, your remaining recovery time decreases by 2 days. Finally, there is a 33 percent chance that you are unable to cast Wish ever again if you suffer this stress.
